bug.actual_behavior: With Windows Rscript locale C, R/knitr output is serialized as <U+XXXX>; Pandoc escapes it to <U+XXXX>, so the HTML displays literal Unicode placeholders.
bug.additional_notes: The issue is in rendering-chain locale/encoding handling, not in bensz-rmd-rules content guidance. Local report only; no public upload requested.
evidence: 02-ablation03-experiment.html initially contained many literal Unicode placeholders; R locale reported C; after document/output hooks decode placeholders and rerender, placeholder counts are zero.
bug.expected_behavior: Rendered HTML should retain real UTF-8 Chinese and other Unicode characters in code output, inline results, and document text.
bug.impact: 这是由 skill 设计缺陷导致的真实环境问题，需要纳入后续修复闭环。
reproduction_steps: Run the knit-rmd-html renderer for a Chinese Rmd on Windows with Rscript locale C.
Include Chinese text in emitted output or inline/document content.
Inspect the generated HTML and observe literal <U+XXXX> or <U+XXXX> placeholders.
bug.summary: R Markdown renderer does not preserve Unicode output when Windows R locale is C
bug.workaround: Set knitr encoding to UTF-8 and decode <U+XXXX> plus HTML-escaped placeholders in knitr output/text/document hooks before Pandoc.
